title: Content model
summary: The content model is the block tables and default content authors type in Word, Docs or Experience Workspace. The same structure becomes the delivered markup, so a good model keeps authoring simple and the HTML meaningful.

items.title: Default content first
items.detail: Use plain headings, paragraphs, images and lists; never make a text, heading or image block.

items.title: No nested blocks
items.detail: Never put a table inside a block cell; use a fragment or an auto-blocked link instead.

items.title: Simple table shape
items.detail: Merge cells only for the block-name header row and keep the number of columns small.

items.title: Block Collection models
items.detail: When a block does the same job as a Block Collection block, reuse that content model.

items.title: Few blocks and variants
items.detail: Infer variants from the content where possible and retire blocks and variants authors rarely use.

items.title: Buttons from context
items.detail: A link alone on a line is a button; bold marks a primary button and italic a secondary one.

items.title: Full URLs
items.detail: Let authors paste fully qualified URLs and let code extract the path it needs.

items.title: Key/value for settings
items.detail: Use name/value rows only for settings that are not displayed, never for headings, images or text.

items.title: No code in documents
items.detail: Authors never type HTML, CSS or JSON; tags or curly braces in a document mean the model is wrong.

title: Experience Workspace
summary: Experience Workspace, formerly Document Authoring (da.live), is the browser editor for EDS document-based content, with layout and content views, sheets and its own configs. Check it before authors start working in it.

items.title: Two kinds of config
items.detail: Keep permissions and library in Experience Workspace configs; CDN, headers and publish roles go in Edge Delivery config.

items.title: Authoring locked down
items.detail: Content is public by default, so set Experience Workspace permissions before inviting authors.

items.title: Publishing protected
items.detail: Preview and publish are open by default; enable author authentication in tools.aem.live.

items.title: Layout view loads
items.detail: head.html loads /scripts/scripts.js and scripts.js defines a top-level loadPage function.

items.title: CORS for preview.da.live
items.detail: Off-origin APIs, fragments and fonts allow the {branch}--{site}--{org}.preview.da.live origin.

items.title: Nested list markup
items.detail: Experience Workspace adds a paragraph inside nested list items; check block code and CSS handle it.

items.title: Preflight enforced
items.detail: Set editor.enforcePreflight to true when content must pass Preflight before publishing.

items.title: Dot folders by URL
items.detail: Folders like /.da and /.helix are hidden in the list view; open them by typing the path.

title: Universal Editor
summary: With AEM authoring (xwalk) or Experience Workspace, the Universal Editor edits EDS pages through component definitions, models and filters in JSON. They decide which blocks authors can add and how form fields become block tables.

items.title: Three JSON files
items.detail: Keep the component definitions, models and filters JSON in the repo root, generated with npm run build:json.

items.title: Block resource and name
items.detail: Each xwalk block uses core/franklin/components/block/v1/block and a block name, or it will not render.

items.title: No custom components
items.detail: Never change or replace the AEM components for EDS; their markup is a fixed contract.

items.title: Block in section filter
items.detail: Add each new block id to the section filter, or authors cannot insert it.

items.title: Semantic field names
items.detail: Use Alt, Text, Title and Type suffixes and group_field names so fields collapse into semantic markup.

items.title: Options as classes
items.detail: Model block options with a classes field or classes_ group instead of new blocks.

items.title: Instrumentation kept
items.detail: When decoration moves content, carry data-aue-* attributes over with moveInstrumentation().

items.title: Multi-field flag reviewed
items.detail: Turn on xwalk multi-field rendering only after checking blocks, since it changes existing markup.

items.title: Branch tested
items.detail: Load the feature branch in the editor with ?ref=<branch> before merging to main.

title: Sidekick
summary: AEM Sidekick is the browser extension authors use to preview, publish, unpublish and switch environments from documents and pages. Set it up so authors sign in, see the right project and only the tools they need.

items.title: Extension installed
items.detail: Authors install AEM Sidekick from the Chrome Web Store; Edge needs extensions from other stores allowed.

items.title: Project added
items.detail: Add the project in Sidekick so it recognizes the production and custom preview domains.

items.title: Sign-in works
items.detail: With roles configured, authors sign in through Sidekick before they can preview or publish.

items.title: Unpublish and delete roles
items.detail: Unpublish needs the publish role and delete needs author or publish; check who holds them.

items.title: Plugins in site config
items.detail: Add custom plugins in the sidekick object of the site configuration, each with a unique id.

items.title: Plugins scoped
items.detail: Use environments, includePaths and excludePaths so each plugin shows only where it applies.

items.title: Bulk actions sized
items.detail: Use bulk preview and publish from SharePoint or Drive; split SharePoint selections above 60 files.

items.title: Enterprise host policy
items.detail: Limit where the extension runs with runtime_blocked_hosts and runtime_allowed_hosts in managed Chrome.

title: Placeholders
summary: Placeholders are a Key/Text sheet of shared UI strings that block code reads as JSON. They keep labels out of code and let each language or locale carry its own wording.

items.title: Sheet named placeholders
items.detail: Create a placeholders sheet in the site root or each locale root (placeholders.xlsx in SharePoint).

items.title: Key and Text columns
items.detail: The sheet has at least a Key column and a Text column.

items.title: Helper copied
items.detail: placeholders.js lives in the Block Collection, not the boilerplate; copy it into scripts/.

items.title: Locale folder passed
items.detail: Call fetchPlaceholders with the page's locale folder; with no argument it loads the root sheet.

items.title: Keys camel-cased
items.detail: Keys become camelCase in code, so about us is aboutUs; avoid keys that collide after conversion.

items.title: No hard-coded labels
items.detail: Move repeated UI strings such as button labels out of block code into placeholders.

items.title: Market overrides
items.detail: Keep most strings in the language folder and override only what differs in a market folder.

items.title: Previewed before publish
items.detail: Preview the sheet and check the strings on .aem.page before publishing it.

title: Bulk metadata
summary: Bulk metadata is a metadata sheet that applies meta tags to many pages by URL pattern, such as a default image, a template or noindex for a folder. Row order and precedence decide what each page ends up with.

items.title: Sheet at content root
items.detail: Name it metadata (metadata.xlsx in SharePoint) in the content root, with a single sheet.

items.title: URL patterns
items.detail: A URL column holds path patterns with * wildcards, such as /docs/** or **/docs/**.

items.title: Broad rows first
items.detail: Rows apply top to bottom, so site-wide ** entries come before more specific ones.

items.title: One column per property
items.detail: Name each column after its property, such as template, theme or robots; names are lower-cased.

items.title: Default share image
items.detail: Set a site-wide image so every page has one for social sharing.

items.title: Page block wins
items.detail: A page's metadata block overrides the sheet, so check pages that should inherit the bulk value.

items.title: Removal with quotes
items.detail: Use "" as a value to remove a tag for a path, such as the canonical link.

items.title: Sheet published
items.detail: Preview and publish the metadata sheet; pages do not change until it is published.

items.title: Extra sheets ordered
items.detail: For several teams, list extra metadata sources in site config; later ones overwrite but never delete.

title: Spreadsheets & JSON
summary: Any sheet previewed from the content source is served as JSON at its .json path, which powers redirects, placeholders, metadata and custom data. Check which tabs are exposed and how big the payload gets.

items.title: Previewed to JSON
items.detail: A sheet is served at its .json path only after preview, and on .aem.live only after publish.

items.title: Header row
items.detail: The first row holds column names; each later row becomes one object in data.

items.title: Exposed tabs chosen
items.detail: In multi-sheet workbooks only shared- tabs are delivered; keep internal tabs unprefixed.

items.title: Private tabs in EW
items.detail: Experience Workspace sheet tabs are public unless the tab name starts with private-.

items.title: Paginated reads
items.detail: Without limit only 1000 rows come back; use limit and offset in code that reads large sheets.

items.title: Payload under limit
items.detail: Keep each JSON response under the 6MB compressed limit by paging large sheets.

items.title: No named single sheet
items.detail: EDS rejects a single named sheet from Experience Workspace; add an empty second sheet or adjust code.

items.title: Arrays parsed
items.detail: Arrays in cells arrive as strings, so JSON.parse them in code.

items.title: Big sheets stay external
items.detail: Keep sheets with formulas or very many rows in SharePoint or Drive through content overlay.

title: In-context editing
summary: Experience Workspace layout view (Canvas, quick edit) renders the page with your real block code and lets authors edit text and images in place. Blocks must keep the markers it adds, or fields stop being editable.

items.title: Entry script found
items.detail: head.html loads /scripts/scripts.js and scripts.js defines a top-level loadPage function.

items.title: Block element kept
items.detail: Change a block's children and add classes, but never replace the block or overwrite its classes.

items.title: Authored text moved
items.detail: Move original elements so data-prose-index survives; never copy text into new elements.

items.title: No decoration inside text
items.detail: Put icons and classes on a wrapper or ancestor CSS, not on headings, paragraphs or list items.

items.title: Descendant selectors
items.detail: Style text with descendant selectors and JS-marked cells, not child or sibling combinators.

items.title: Image attributes kept
items.detail: Copy data-image-* to optimized images and keep authored images as pictures, not CSS backgrounds.

items.title: Safe to re-run
items.detail: Scope timers and listeners to the block and guard global handlers, since loadPage runs again.

items.title: Idempotent auto-blocks
items.detail: buildAutoBlocks checks for an existing block before adding one.

items.title: Layout view edit test
items.detail: Type in each text field, replace each image and move the block in layout view before merging.

title: Block library
summary: The library is the set of blocks, templates, icons and placeholders authors insert from Experience Workspace, built from example documents and sheets and wired up in the site config. A tidy library is how authors learn the content model.

items.title: One document per block
items.detail: Create a document per block under library/blocks, its header row holding the block name.

items.title: Variants labeled
items.detail: Show visual variants as block (variant) and label content variants with a heading above the table.

items.title: Descriptions added
items.detail: Add a library-metadata block with a description where blocks are easy to confuse.

items.title: Blocks sheet
items.detail: A blocks sheet in the library folder lists name and path for every block document.

items.title: Library tab in config
items.detail: The site config has a library tab pointing to the blocks, templates, placeholders and icons JSON.

items.title: Authors read CONFIG
items.detail: Grant authors read on /{site}/CONFIG, or the block library will not load for them.

items.title: Metadata options
items.detail: Predefine section-metadata and metadata values in block options so authors pick instead of type.

items.title: Rare blocks hidden
items.detail: Keep developer-placed or rarely used blocks out of the main library.

items.title: Author walkthrough
items.detail: As an author, insert each block from the library and check it renders.

title: Translation & locales
summary: EDS favors language-first folders with market folders only where content differs. Experience Workspace's Translate app sends pages to Google Translate or a connector and rolls them out to locales, driven by a translate config sheet.

items.title: Strategy chosen
items.detail: Pick language-, region-, locale-based or hybrid structure before setting up translation.

items.title: Language-first URLs
items.detail: Put language first and market second, such as /en/ and /en/uk/, to limit duplicate content.

items.title: Translate config sheet
items.detail: Set service, languages and rules in /.da/translate; without it Google Translate defaults apply.

items.title: Do-not-translate rules
items.detail: Protect product names, paths and settings blocks with do-not-translate rules.

items.title: Merge for local edits
items.detail: Use merge for rollouts when regional teams edit their own pages, so edits survive updates.

items.title: Secrets kept apart
items.detail: Store connector credentials in a separate translate-keys sheet with tighter access.

items.title: Sources previewed
items.detail: Pages in a translation project must be previewed or published and in the same site.

items.title: Hreflang alternates
items.detail: List each page's language versions with hreflang alternates in the sitemap.

items.title: Visitor chooses market
items.detail: Let visitors pick language and market and remember it, instead of relying on detection.

title: Access & roles
summary: Who can edit is set in Experience Workspace permissions; who can preview, publish or read origin content is set by Edge Delivery roles in the site config. Set both on purpose before authors and integrations get access.

items.title: Both layers set
items.detail: Set edit rights in Experience Workspace and preview and publish rights in Edge Delivery config.

items.title: CONFIG row present
items.detail: Always include a CONFIG write row for admins so nobody is locked out of the config.

items.title: Groups over emails
items.detail: Grant access to IMS orgs and groups where you have Admin Console, not individual emails.

items.title: Path rules tested
items.detail: Rules match the longest path per group and union across groups; test drafts and locked folders.

items.title: Roles mapped
items.detail: Map author and publish roles to users or *@domain in the site's access.admin config.

items.title: requireAuth decided
items.detail: Choose auto, true or false on purpose; mapping roles under auto forces sign-in.

items.title: Least privilege
items.detail: Give publish only to people who ship; keep develop, config_admin and admin to a few.

items.title: API keys scoped
items.detail: Create Admin API keys with only the roles they need, store them safely and rotate before expiry.

items.title: Sensitive folders locked
items.detail: None hides content but not names in lists; stage sensitive work in a fully locked folder.
